title: Minimum Adjacent Swaps to Alternate Parity
summary: Given an array of distinct integers, determine the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to transform the array into a valid arrangement where the parity of adjacent elements alternates (i.e., each pair of adjacent elements consists of one even and one odd number).
statement: Given an array of distinct integers, determine the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to transform the array into a valid arrangement where the parity of adjacent elements alternates (i.e., each pair of adjacent elements consists of one even and one odd number). If it is impossible to achieve such an arrangement, return -1.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 distinct positive integers.
Only adjacent swaps are allowed, and adjacent parities must alternate in the result.
Return the minimum swaps, or -1 when parity counts differ by more than one.
hints: Stable ordering within each parity is optimal because crossing equal-parity elements only adds swaps.
Match parity positions in order to the alternating slots for each feasible starting parity.
Reject count imbalance; sum absolute position differences to slots 0,2,4,... and minimize when both starts are possible.
Each unit of displacement corresponds to one crossing with the opposite parity, and ordered matching minimizes total displacement without unnecessary same-parity crossings.
editorial: Each unit of displacement corresponds to one crossing with the opposite parity, and ordered matching minimizes total displacement without unnecessary same-parity crossings.
